title: P4-14: port video-script loading in the GraphQL content repository (article/edition video scripts)
description: P4-03 (Papyrus#150) moved the blog layout components and added the optional videoScripts field on EditionContent, passed through the rhythm renderers, but the fork video-script loading in the GraphQL content repository (how Threat Intelligence loads edition/article video scripts from the backend) is NOT ported. Threat Intelligence uses edition/article videos (baseline has a PLAY VIDEO button and edition video blocks). Port the loader generically (any brand with videoPlayer set), with tests against the content model, so a publication on the packages shows the same videos as the fork. Check what data the old backend holds (baseline: ~/Projects/.baselines/threat-intelligence-20261007/) and that the P4-08/P4-09 copy tool carries the video-script fields. Also carry the figure.article-video margin-bottom 2em rule in the TI theme (P4-04).

comments.author: home
comments.text: Merged Papyrus#154 (squash 6039c627). Fork loads scripts in lib/graphql-content-repository.ts (loadVideoScript, loadEditionVideoScripts) reading PublishedItem rows of type `videoml` with slug `<target>--videoml` and `editorial.videoScript.{dsl,target.kind}`; targets = `edition-overview` (if editionVideo) plus each item with a video; dev-only gate shouldFetchVideoScripts. Ported generically (gated on brand videoPlayer) with loadVideoScript on the repository contract, EditionContent.videoScripts, getCachedVideoScript, /articles/[slug] pass-through, collectVideoScriptTargets test in test:video-script. No schema change (Item/PublishedItem already have type string + editorial json). Old TI backend baseline holds 0 videoml items (Item: 18 article + 2 doctrine; PublishedItem 18 article), so TI videos are MediaAsset mp4 + editionVideo metadata; nothing extra to copy. Left open: the figure.article-video margin-bottom 2em rule in the TI theme belongs to the TI repo (P4-04).

right_now_summary: Video-script loading is ported and tested; only the TI theme’s video margin rule remains.
